summary: Offer only host-usable named CPU models in Inventory.cpu_models (libvirt domain capabilities usable=yes) and define named models with check=partial so KVM extras no longer block start.

guide.reason: Create and edit guides now say the CPU selector lists models this host can run, not every QEMU name.

api.reason: Inventory.cpu_models is filtered to libvirt usable=yes models on q35; named VMCPU.model definitions use check=partial instead of check=full. Auth, operations and adoption are unchanged. Existing VMs keep their stored XML until edited.

state.reason: Selected CPU model remains pool-scoped VM configuration on the master; cpu_models stays a read-only Core observation.
state.record: The selected model remains in the managed journal and returns through Inventory.managed.vms for re-adoption. Inventory.cpu_models is discovered from the assigned host's domain capabilities and is never Controller-owned state.

verification.method: Focused Go tests for usableCPUModels parsing, named-model XML check=partial, and availableCPUModel domain-capabilities query. Live host earlier confirmed qemu64/Nehalem fail check=full and succeed check=partial; domcapabilities usable filter drops ~107 unusable models on au-matthome.
